body_text:
Fundamental theorem of calculus, evaluation form. If
$f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuous and $G:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ is
continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$ with $G'=f$,
then $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=G(b)-G(a)$. Any two antiderivatives differ
by a constant on the interval.
